criteria.rationale:
I checked every named framework API against the digest and my own knowledge.

Deployment targets are iOS 18.0 and watchOS 11.0, and the SayoneCore package's minimums are lower, which is valid. That target leaves these APIs needing no #available checks: AccessoryWidgetGroup, accessoryWidgetGroupStyle and handGestureShortcut (watchOS 11); promptsForUserConfiguration, ControlWidget, ControlWidgetButton, AppIntentControlConfiguration and ControlConfigurationIntent (iOS 18); the iOS 18 / watchOS 11 AppEntity @Parameter init; and DisplayRepresentation(title:subtitle:image:synonyms:) (iOS 17 / watchOS 10).

The only APIs newer than the deployment targets are both correctly gated:
- recommendations() returning [] sits behind `if #available(watchOS 26.0, *)`.
- The watch-native control is explicitly deferred.

The cross-platform traps the digest flags are all handled:
- .accessoryCorner and .system* family lists are split with #if os().
- A `default:` case is required in every WidgetFamily switch.
- recommendations() is implemented under #if os(watchOS), where it is mandatory; iOS has a default.
- promptsForUserConfiguration on the widget is inside #if os(iOS).
- ShortcutsLink is iOS-only.
- The WCSession inactive/deactivate delegate methods and isWatchAppInstalled are iOS-only.
- LiveActivityIntent is behind #if os(iOS) && INTENTS_IN_APP_PROCESS.
- The control content closure holds only `let` statements plus one ControlWidgetButton.
- ControlConfigurationIntent's parameter is optional.
- Widget intents take only pre-filled primitive parameters, each with a default.

The proposal forbids openAppWhenRun, supportedModes, ForegroundContinuableIntent, allowedExecutionTargets, earliestAuthorizedSampleDate, HKCorrelation, handleAuthorizationForExtension and HealthKitUI. The HealthKit APIs it uses (the descriptor queries, statusForAuthorizationRequest, the async save/delete/deleteObjects, HKQuantityType(.x)) all match the digest.

The APIs outside the digest are listed in §20: WatchConnectivity updateApplicationContext and receivedApplicationContext, MeasurementFormatter, os.Logger, isPreview and xcconfig `#include?`. All are long-available APIs from iOS 9/10/14 and watchOS 2/3/7, and I can confirm them from my own knowledge. None is an unguarded newer API.

Capabilities are HealthKit and App Groups only. The Siri, push, iCloud and associated-domains entitlements are forbidden and lint-checked.

The project is reproducible. XcodeGen 2.46.0 is pinned, and I ran the §14.2 project.yml through the Linux XcodeGen 2.46.0 build. It generated cleanly with:
- one Embed Watch Content phase and two Embed Foundation Extensions phases
- both shared schemes
- IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET 18.0 and WATCHOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET 11.0
- the Cyrillic INAlternativeAppNames serialized correctly

SWIFT_VERSION is 5.0 with minimal strict concurrency, MainActor default isolation is left off, and the generated .xcodeproj is committed.

There are two small issues, neither of which is an unverified or unguarded framework API:
1. The contract has the nonisolated CatalogSync WCSessionDelegate call `AppModel.applyReceivedCatalog` synchronously, and AppModel is @MainActor. I verified with swiftc 6.4 `-swift-version 5` that this is an ERROR even in Swift 5 mode, so the contract must say to hop through Task { @MainActor in }.
2. The preflight `grep` counts would not match the real pbxproj line counts.

The INTENTS_IN_APP_PROCESS escape hatch is compiled only in a continue-on-error step, which is weak but not a defect.

The pass anchor holds.

criteria.rationale:
Checking each item of the pass anchor:

1. App Shortcuts with Russian and English phrases: yes. SayoneShortcuts is an AppShortcutsProvider with 4 AppShortcuts, each with shortTitle and systemImageName. Phrases are in AppShortcuts.xcstrings with en and ru stringSets. Each key is the first English phrase, and each phrase contains ${applicationName} exactly once, which is lint-enforced. The Russian variants cover gender (выпил/выпила) and case forms.

2. Parameterised by drink or preset: yes.
- LogDrinkIntent takes a DrinkEntity. Its DrinkQuery is an EntityStringQuery with suggestedEntities, the entities carry accusative synonyms, and updateAppShortcutParameters() is called after catalog changes.
- LogWaterIntent takes a WaterAmount AppEnum (glass, can, half-litre, litre). Its ru titles are chosen so that «Запиши пол-литра воды» reads naturally.
- Each phrase has at most one parameter, and there are no Int or Measurement parameters in phrases.

3. Runs without opening the app: yes. No openAppWhenRun or supportedModes is declared, and Siri intents run in the background in the app process. If Health is not authorized, the entry is journaled and Siri speaks a dialog.

4. Available on the watch: yes. The provider, the intents and both catalogs are compiled into the watch app, and updateAppShortcutParameters() is called in the watch App.init(). INAlternativeAppNames is repeated in the watch plist. CI asserts the autoShortcuts in the embedded watch app's extract.actionsdata.

5. Today's-total query intent: yes. TodayTotalIntent answers with a dialog («Сегодня 1,2 л из 2 л.»), computed from the snapshot and the journal, so it works while the device is locked.

6. No SiriKit: correct. No com.apple.developer.siri entitlement and no Intents extension; this is lint-enforced.

There is also an UndoLastIntent App Shortcut.

Minor weaknesses that don't affect the anchor:
- The "Log water in X" / "Запиши воду в X" phrases (LogWaterIntent) overlap with "Log ${drink}" / "Запиши ${drink}" when the drink is Water or its synonym «воду». This is ambiguous but harmless, since both log water.
- The «Какой напиток?» prompt needs a requestValueDialog, which the contract omits.

Every element is present, so this is a pass.

must_fix: §7/§16.6: CatalogSync is a nonisolated NSObject/WCSessionDelegate, yet it calls the @MainActor AppModel.shared.applyReceivedCatalog synchronously from didReceiveApplicationContext. I verified with swiftc 6.4 -swift-version 5: this is a hard error ('call to main actor-isolated instance method ... in a synchronous nonisolated context'), even in Swift 5 mode with minimal checking. The contract should require `Task { @MainActor in AppModel.shared.applyReceivedCatalog(catalog) }`, and should not mark the delegate witnesses @MainActor.

§14.5 preflight: the pattern `Embed Watch Content */ = {` also matches PBXBuildFile lines ('X.app in Embed Watch Content */ = {'). I generated the §14.2 spec with XcodeGen 2.46.0: `grep -c` then returns 2 for Embed Watch Content and 4 for Embed Foundation Extensions, not the expected 1 and 2. Match only the phase definition lines (the 24-hex id followed directly by /* Embed ... */) or change the expected counts, otherwise the Linux preflight fails on a correct project.
best_ideas: Set the deployment targets to iOS 18 / watchOS 11. This removes almost every #available check (interactive watch widgets, AccessoryWidgetGroup, handGestureShortcut, Controls, promptsForUserConfiguration). Only two watchOS 26 branches are left, plus a documented watchOS 10 fallback.

Add a lint.py `#if` state tracker that enforces per-platform symbol allow-lists and forbidden symbols per folder. Put requestAuthorization only in Shared/AppOnly, so extensions cannot even compile a HealthKit prompt.

Add check_appintents.py to assert autoShortcuts in both the iOS app and the embedded watch app's Metadata.appintents, and to assert that no widget .appex carries autoShortcuts. It should also fail on 'No AppIntents metadata have been exported'.
Lint AppShortcuts.xcstrings: ${applicationName} appears exactly once per phrase, placeholders come from a whitelist, each key equals the first Swift phrase, and there are at most 10 AppShortcuts.

Make the WaterAmount AppEnum's ru case titles (стакан/банку/пол-литра/литр) fit the template «Запиши ${amount} воды». Spoken amounts then work with no Int or Measurement phrase parameter, which matters on the watch where matching is exact.

Add a compile-flag escape hatch (INTENTS_IN_APP_PROCESS makes the intent a LiveActivityIntent on iOS only) that CI builds. It gives a known-compiling fallback in case HealthKit saves from the widget extension fail on the device.
Use a staged bring-up: before parallel lanes branch, the macOS job must pass with every contract present as a compiling stub. Run swiftc -parse and xcodegen on Linux before every push.
Defer the watch-native control, because the iOS 18 control already appears on watchOS 26. This keeps limited-availability WidgetBundleBuilder paths out of v1.
Add UndoLastIntent and TodayTotalIntent as App Shortcuts, so Siri can also undo the last drink and read back today's total.

criteria.rationale:
I checked each of the five data properties against the proposal text.

(1) Idempotent HealthKit writes: covered concretely. Every sample carries HKMetadataKeySyncIdentifier "<UUID>.<component>", unique per sample type, plus HKMetadataKeySyncVersion NSNumber(1), always paired. Retries and double flushes reuse the same id and version, and both success and an error on re-save count as saved. This matches the verified facts.

(2) No watch/phone double counting: covered structurally. Each entry is written to HealthKit only by the device that was tapped. HealthKit is the only channel that carries entries between devices; WatchConnectivity carries only the catalog, one way. The same drink therefore never reaches Health twice, and no WatchConnectivity entry merge exists that could double count. Within one device, today's total is a HealthKit snapshot plus local pending entries plus entries saved after the snapshot's readAt, minus pendingDelete entries. This overlay is time-based and has race windows: readAt is captured before the query, and §5.2 sets healthSavedAt = now, i.e. the log time. A sample that commits concurrently can be counted twice or dropped. That error is transient and fixes itself on the next read, so this is not double counting by construction.

(3) Undo/delete removes Health samples: covered. There is a pendingDelete status that is hidden from totals at once, deleteObjects with a SayoneEntryID predicate for each component, a flush retry, a 30-minute UndoPolicy, and UndoLastIntent reachable from the app, the iOS widget and Siri. A row from the other device gets a delete attempt and, if 0 samples are removed, an honest .notDeletableHere message. It is not routed over WatchConnectivity, so a user cannot delete the other device's entry from here. Two defects: deleting a `.pending` entry removes only the file, and the logger's post-save rewrite can bring a deleted entry back.

(4) Locked-device and extension writes not lost: covered. The journal file is written first and atomically, using the default complete-until-first-authentication protection (never .complete). The HealthKit save is best effort. On error the entry stays pending and is flushed when the app becomes active or after the next successful save. Extensions never prompt for authorization. The iOS-only LiveActivityIntent escape hatch is compiled in CI.

(5) Widget, phone and watch totals converge: covered, eventually. HealthKit is the shared source of truth; widgets reload after every log and refresh every 30 minutes and at midnight; the app refreshes whenever it becomes active; a snapshot cache covers locked reads. There is no push to the other device's widget when HealthKit sync lands, so a total can be stale for up to about 30 minutes plus sync latency. Convergence also silently depends on the user granting read permission for dietaryWater on both devices, which the proposal never mentions: with share-only access, each device sees only its own bundle's samples.

All five properties have concrete mechanisms, so the score is pass. The race and tombstone defects are real and listed under must_fix, which is why I marked this ambiguous.

criteria.rationale:
The module boundaries are explicit and layered. SayoneCore is pure and Linux-tested. Above it sit Shared/Core (Apple services), then Shared/Intents, then Shared/WidgetUI and Shared/AppOnly, then the per-target folders. A target-membership matrix lists exactly which folder compiles into which of the 4 targets. The dependency rules are lint-enforced: forbidden symbols per folder, so requestAuthorization cannot compile into extensions, plus platform-gating lists.

§16 gives exact signatures for every shared type: package public API, Shared/Core services, intents, widget providers, AppModel and the Siri types. They are frozen after a skeleton stage in which every contract exists as a compiling stub that must be green on macOS CI before lanes branch.

§17 defines 6 lanes with file-ownership scopes and dependencies, plus a documented merge down to 4 engineers. Even the localization catalogs are split into per-lane fragments merged by a generator, which avoids xcstrings merge conflicts. Contract changes go through E1 as stub updates.

The architecture itself stays reasonably simple: one logging path for every surface, no entry-sync protocol, one-way WatchConnectivity for the catalog only, and no third-party dependencies. Coupling is limited: AppModel is shared by both apps and owned by E4 while E5 depends on its contract, and AppModel.edit calls SayoneShortcuts from E6. Both dependencies are covered by the stubs. This meets the pass anchor.

criteria.rationale:
All data stays on the devices or within Apple services. Storage is the App Group JSON files per device and HealthKit. WatchConnectivity carries only the drink/preset catalog between the user's own devices. There is no network code, analytics or third-party dependency.

NSHealthShareUsageDescription and NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription are declared on all 4 targets, including the widget extensions, and are localized (en/ru) in both apps.

Only the needed HealthKit types are requested. The share set is water, caffeine, energy and sugar, each of which is actually written (nutrients behind a user toggle). The read set is dietaryWater only. com.apple.developer.healthkit.access is an empty array, so clinical records are never requested. No correlation types are used.

The proposal makes no medical claims. It states that nutrient values are approximate and editable and that the UI makes no medical claims. A per-drink 'hydration' factor exists, but it is a plain, user-editable coefficient.

The deep link opens a confirmation sheet and never auto-logs, so an external URL cannot write Health data without the user confirming. DEVELOPMENT_TEAM lives in a gitignored Local.xcconfig, so the public repository does not leak the user's team id.

must_fix: §5.1/§5.2 cross-process lost update. After HealthGateway.save returns, DrinkLogger step 4 and flush write Journal/<uuid>.json back as `.saved` without re-reading it. If another process (the app's undo/delete, Siri, or the other flush) set `.pendingDelete` or removed the file in the meantime, this write brings the deleted entry back and the Health sample stays. The claim 'processes write different files, no lost updates, no file coordination' is false for status transitions. Fix: after the save, re-read the file. If it is missing or `.pendingDelete`, do not write it; call deleteSamples(entryID:) instead. Otherwise write it. NSFileCoordinator is an alternative. Never downgrade pendingDelete.

§5.3 delete/undo of a `.pending` entry only removes the file. `.pending` does not prove that no Health sample exists: the save may still be running in the widget-extension or Siri process, the process may have been killed between the save and the status write, or the save may have committed and then returned an error. The result is a Health sample left behind while the UI says the drink was undone, and the in-flight logger then re-creates the file. Fix: treat pending like saved. Mark it `.pendingDelete`, run deleteSamples(entryID:) (which harmlessly returns 0 when nothing is there), then remove the file. flush must never re-save a pendingDelete entry.

§5.4 TodayMath races, and a stale snapshot after delete. (a) Comparing healthSavedAt with readAt cannot tell whether a concurrently committed sample is inside the statistics result, because readAt is captured before the query. If healthSavedAt is taken after the save, the sample is counted twice; if it is the log time (§5.2 writes `healthSavedAt = now`, where `now` is the log time), it drops out. (b) Once the HealthKit delete succeeds, the file is removed and the `sub` term no longer applies, while the cached snapshot still contains the sample. The deleted drink reappears in the total until the next successful HealthKit read (DrinkLogger.delete does not refresh the snapshot, and locked or failed reads keep the old one). Fix: store `othersML` in the snapshot, meaning today's HealthKit sum minus this device's own samples (query by SayoneOrigin == ThisDevice.kind or by SayoneEntryID). Compute total = othersML + Σ today's non-deleted local entries, with no timestamps involved. Alternatively, keep deleted tombstones until a snapshot with readAt > deletedAt exists. Add Linux unit tests for both cases.

§6 deletion calls deleteObjects(of:) for every component type. If a type such as caffeine is not share-authorized, the call throws an authorization error. The entry then stays `.queued`/pendingDelete forever and flush retries it endlessly, and depending on loop order the water sample may never be deleted. Fix: filter the types by writeAuth == .authorized, delete water on its own first, and treat an authorization error on a nutrient type as done.

§5.1 when catalog.json is corrupt, CatalogStore.load() falls back to Catalog.makeDefault(), which resets `revision`. The watch ignores lower revisions (§7), so the phone's later edits never reach the watch until the revision climbs past the old value. Fix: on fallback, set revision = max(.bak revision, current epoch milliseconds), or have the watch compare `updatedAt`.

§5.2 `drink = catalog.drink(id) ?? BuiltInCatalog.drink(.water)` silently logs an unknown drinkID (for example after a catalog reset) as water, with the wrong name and nutrients, into Health. Fix: carry the drink name and snapshot values in QuickLogIntent/PresetEntity and use them, or log nothing and surface an error.

Cross-device totals silently depend on Health READ permission for dietaryWater on both devices. With share-only access, HealthKit returns only the calling source's samples, so the phone never sees samples from the watch bundle and vice versa, and the totals never converge. Read denial cannot be detected, so onboarding, the README and the §19 test plan must tell the user to allow reading Water on both the iPhone and the watch.

Minor: the History local fallback uses localDailyTotals(days: 7), but saved journal entries are pruned after 3 days, so days 4–7 show 0 whenever the HealthKit read fails. Fix: keep the journal for at least 7 days, or label the fallback as partial.
best_ideas: Each entry is written to HealthKit only by the device that was tapped, and HealthKit is the only channel that carries entries between devices. This removes the need for a WatchConnectivity entry-sync protocol and the double counting it could cause. WatchConnectivity is used only for the catalog, one way from phone to watch, with a revision number where the latest wins.

One JSON file per journal entry in the App Group (Journal/<uuid>.json), written atomically with default protection (complete until first user authentication). The entry is written to the journal before the HealthKit save is attempted, so no tap is lost on a locked device or in an extension. Add a re-read-before-status-write guard to make it race-free.

Per-component sync identifiers "<UUID>.<component>" plus SyncVersion NSNumber(1), and a filter on authorizationStatus == .sharingAuthorized before the all-or-nothing save([HKObject]), so a denied caffeine permission never drops the water sample.

A health status of pending | saved | pendingDelete on each entry. pendingDelete is hidden from totals immediately and finished later by flush. Deletes are routed to the device that wrote the entry, with an honest .notDeletableHere message when that is not this device.

The today total is pure logic in the Linux-tested package, with a HealthKit snapshot cache for locked or unauthorized reads. Improve it by caching 'others' (the HealthKit total minus this device's own samples) and adding the local journal on top.

The widget and control intent carries only primitive drinkID and volumeML values that default to water/250. Drinks are archived, never deleted, so a configured widget or complication stays valid after presets change.
The deep link opens a confirmation sheet and never logs automatically. This prevents double logging on watchOS 10 or a missed hit target, and stops external URLs from writing Health data.
UndoPolicy (30-minute window) is shared by the in-app toast, the iOS widget undo button and a Siri UndoLastIntent.

Layered folders (Shared/Core → Shared/Intents → Shared/WidgetUI | Shared/AppOnly), a target-membership matrix, and lint-enforced forbidden symbols per folder, so requestAuthorization and WCSession cannot compile into extensions.

§16 contracts are frozen as compiling stubs in a skeleton CI stage before parallel lanes branch. Lanes own disjoint files, and per-lane Localization/*.json fragments are merged into Localizable.xcstrings by a generator with a --check step in CI.
The INTENTS_IN_APP_PROCESS escape hatch (LiveActivityIntent under #if os(iOS)) is compiled in the CI device build, so the fallback is known to build before device testing.
The read set is only dietaryWater and healthkit.access is an empty array: minimal HealthKit scope with clear usage strings on all 4 targets.

criteria.rationale: I checked each requirement for a concrete component and flow. (1) Tap-to-log: the iPhone PresetGrid ('tap = log'), the watch PresetRow ('tap = log + .sensoryFeedback'), and the widget and complication buttons all call one DrinkLogger.log(drinkID:volumeML:) path (§5.2). (2) Drink choice: seven built-in drinks including water and «Кола без сахара»/Cola Zero, plus custom drinks through CatalogEditor.addCustomDrink, DrinkEditorView and LogDrinkSheet. The watch has DrinkPickerView and a Digital Crown VolumePickerView. (3) Every entry reaches Apple Health: the journal is written first, then HealthGateway.save with flat HKQuantitySamples. Pending entries are flushed when either app becomes active, and both devices request authorization in onboarding. (4) Apple Watch app: a single-target app with named screens (WatchRootView, VolumePickerView, ConfirmLogView, WatchOnboardingView). (5) Watch widget and complication: a family-by-family layout table (circular, corner, rectangular, inline, plus a Favorites AccessoryWidgetGroup). (6) One-tap preset configuration: AppIntentConfiguration with SelectPresetIntent(preset: PresetEntity?), Button(intent: QuickLogIntent(drinkID:volumeML:)), watch recommendations() before watchOS 26 and [] from 26, and promptsForUserConfiguration on iOS. The default presets include Water 500 and Cola Zero 330, which match the user's examples. (7) Siri: four App Shortcuts, ru and en phrases in AppShortcuts.xcstrings, and a WaterAmount enum covering «пол-литра». Every requirement maps to a concrete component and flow, and none is vague. One product deviation does not remove coverage: dietaryWater is written as volume × hydrationFactor, so juice and milk record 90% of the poured volume. Water and Cola Zero use 1.0, and the factor can be edited.

criteria.rationale: Watch face one-tap: accessoryCircular and accessoryCorner complications are each a single Button(intent: QuickLogIntent). The rectangular layout adds .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction), and the watchOS 11 deployment target makes the watch widgets interactive. The proposal avoids the AccessoryWidgetBackground-in-.plain hit-test bug. iPhone one-tap: a systemSmall QuickLog button, Lock Screen circular and rectangular widgets that are each one whole-view button, a Favorites systemMedium widget with four preset buttons, and an iOS 18 configurable Control that also shows on watchOS 26. Visible confirmation: perform() waits for the store write before returning, so WidgetKit's reload updates the ring and total. The iPhone app shows a 5 s toast «Записано · Отменить», the watch shows a LoggedBanner with a success haptic, and a pending entry still counts toward the total when the HealthKit write fails. Undo: an UndoLastIntent button on the iPhone small widget appears while the 30-minute window is open, and the timeline refreshes when that window ends. Undo is also in the in-app toast, the watch banner, and Siri «Отмени последний напиток». Per-instance preset configuration: iPhone uses Edit Widget plus promptsForUserConfiguration, watchOS 11 uses one recommendation per preset («Вода · 500 мл»), and watchOS 26 lets the user edit the parameter. The control takes an optional configuration intent. Watch UI: a List-based root with preset rows, the crown picker is kept outside any List and gets .focusable, and the deep-link ConfirmLogView never logs automatically, so the widgetURL fallback cannot double-log. The watch complication has no undo on the complication itself; undo there is only in the app or by voice. The pass anchor requires undo to exist, not undo on every surface, so the criterion is met. One caution: step 4 of §5.2 runs `await flush(limit: 10)` inside the widget's perform(). This adds latency before confirmation on the one-tap path, but it does not break the flow.

best_ideas: Deep-link fallback (widgetURL) opens a confirm-and-log screen that never logs automatically. This covers watchOS 10 and taps that miss the complication button, and it cannot record a drink twice.
iOS systemSmall widget shows a small UndoLastIntent button only while the 30-minute undo window is open, and the timeline policy includes the undo-expiry time so the button disappears on schedule.

Watch Smart Stack Favorites widget: an AccessoryWidgetGroup with the first three presets as one-tap buttons, plus .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction) on the rectangular QuickLog so a double tap logs.
The default preset order puts Water 250, Water 500 and Cola Zero 330 first, so the watch favorites and watch recommendations match the user's examples out of the box.

WaterAmount AppEnum case titles are Russian inflected forms that fit the phrase literally («стакан», «банку», «пол-литра», «литр»), so «Запиши пол-литра воды в …» works with the exact matching the watch requires.
Watch recommendations() descriptions are built as String variables («Вода · 500 мл»), and invalidateConfigurationRecommendations() is called when the phone pushes a new catalog.
The one-tap widget and control intent (QuickLogIntent) takes fully pre-filled primitive parameters with defaults, and the Siri intents are separate types that can prompt.
An iOS-only INTENTS_IN_APP_PROCESS LiveActivityIntent escape hatch is compiled in CI, so switching widget intents to the app process on the device is a tested, flag-only change.
The Ultra Action button is covered with no extra code by the watch app's App Shortcut («Записать воду»).
